evidence.detail: In the hash-matched census bundle the reportSubscribe component calls this route to load its table rows and page_info.total_number. Creating, editing, deleting and exporting a subscription each go through their own separate routes, so listing carries no write side effect.

The recovered frontend builder sends only an integer app_id and the fixed subject "$lib_version", carries no pagination, and the response is consumed as a read-only dictionary of string arrays. No mutation control flow reaches this route.
A minimum single-page request returned HTTP 200 with a semantically successful empty envelope, with no confirmation step, no layout update and no success toast.

The recovered frontend builder proves five top-level fields and seven filter subkeys, and the caller slices the returned list locally. Listing and slicing are read behaviour; no write control flow invokes this route.
A minimum first-page request returned HTTP 200 with a semantically successful empty data.list envelope, with no confirmation step and no modification feedback.

In the hash-matched appManageIndex bundle the Project component calls this route on mount, search, page change and page-size change to populate a project table from data.list and page_info.total_number. Project creation and confirmed deletion use the separate /user/project/create/ mutation route, so this list call has no write side effect.
The extracted exact-route consumers read data.list, item id/name/app_list_info and page_info; the request body is limited to page, page_size and optional name filters.

In hash-matched MasterkeyAd-BgxTfClc.js, the Group component invokes this route on mount, search and page changes with date_list, filters, order_by, page and page_size; it assigns response list rows to the report table and page_info.total_number to the paginator. The route has no mutation feedback or write continuation.

The hash-matched csj and tobid bundles open a RelationAppDrawer from a selected account-list row, pass rowData.account with a fixed monetization_platform value, and call this route to load the drawer's platform-app table. Sync, association and deletion use separate sync_app and app/edit mutation routes.

The two extracted call sites bind account, the fixed csj/tobid platform value, page and page_size; the UI consumes platform app, app type, package name and Gravity-app association fields as table rows.

In hash-matched ReportCommonHeader-Ck1C9MQA.js, opening the saved-report dialog loads this route, renders response list rows and page_info.total_number, and reloads it on page or filter changes. Deletion uses the separate /datamanageconfig/report/update/ route with is_delete=1.

In hash-matched NewReportCenter-Dxgo5EkI.js, MetricsPanel loads this route alongside the normal and owned custom-metric lists, assigns its response list to the shared-metric collection, merges it into the displayed metric catalog, and paginates the merged rows locally. Delete and share mutations use separate routes.

In hash-matched GeneralImportAd-CKb38unY.js, the Ad component invokes this route on mount, search, sort and page changes, assigns response list rows to the table, and consumes page_info.total_number in the paginator. app_id comes from AppSelect and ad_platform from the frontend's finite media-platform options; blank selectors are converted to undefined. Upload and delete use separate routes.

In hash-matched Dashboard-DrzT0Orh.js, the Dashboard page calls this GET with app_id during initial load and App changes, reduces the returned space/folder/dashboard tree into selectable dashboard rows, selects an existing dashboard, and then invokes the separate dashboard-detail GET. Create, rename, move, share, transfer and delete actions use separate routes.

In hash-matched NewReportCenter-Dxgo5EkI.js, ReportDetail invokes this route after loading or refreshing a monetization report, unwraps data.list/data.total (or data.extra_data.accumulate_data), and renders the rows, warning and local sort state. Report and template saves use separate create/edit routes; this call has no confirmation, persistence continuation or mutation feedback.

The extracted exact call site contains nine top-level body fields and no query or page fields; the shared table paginates the returned full list locally and displays an empty state when the consumed row array has no items.

In hash-matched Dashboard-DrzT0Orh.js, selecting a tree item calls this GET with app_id, dashboard id and space_id, consumes ui_config as JSON, and stores the returned dashboard detail for rendering. Layout saves and report-setting changes call separate POST routes and display their own success feedback.

In hash-matched Dashboard-DrzT0Orh.js, opening the add-chart flow calls this GET with app_id, optional subject filters, page and page_size, consumes response list rows, and JSON-parses a selected row's config before adding it locally. Saving the dashboard or changing a report uses separate POST routes.

Across eight hash-matched Analysis page bundles, opening an existing saved analysis calls this GET with app_id and id, requires the returned config, JSON-parses it, and restores the analysis form plus name/remark display state. Saving edits uses the separate report_config/update POST route.

In hash-matched NewReportCenter-Dxgo5EkI.js, ReportDetail calls calc_total only after the main result has loaded and a client-side condition or pivot needs totals recomputed, or when local filtering/row expansion changes. It sends already loaded row groups and uses only data.list to replace local summary or pivot rows; no server resource is created, edited or deleted.

The extracted exact call site contains eight top-level body fields, including data_list, and no query or page fields. The call is awaited sequentially rather than dispatched as an unconditional companion to the main report query.

In hash-matched Measurement-BV1Ulzee.js, clicking Search invokes the attribution route four times with aggregate metric/dimension profiles, then consumes data.items and data.total to populate natural/promoted charts and conversion summary cards. Saved-report persistence uses separate ReportCommonHeader routes, and this call has no confirmation, write continuation or mutation feedback.

The recovered builder has fourteen always-emitted top-level keys, two conditional keys and a fixed eight-list filtering object. The direct-App natural/promoted activation call has no pagination or attribution-scheme parent and uses the catalog App id plus fixed frontend metric/dimension/caliber values.
